## Customer impact assessment: Incident 2026-08-21

**Endpoint affected:** `POST /checkout` — this is the purchase-completion path, so every affected request is a customer who could not complete an order, not a degraded-but-working experience.

**Severity:** Sev1, per the document header.

**Total window:** 14:02–14:47 UTC (45 minutes), with the doc separately noting error rate reached 0% "within two minutes" of the 14:47 fix, so full recovery lands around 14:49.

---

### Phase-by-phase

**Phase 0 — 13:58 to 14:02 (pre-impact, 4 min)**
`v412` begins rolling out across four instances, one at a time. No customer-facing error yet. This is the incubation period: the config bundle carrying `PAYMENTS_SETTLEMENT_MODE: split` is already in flight, but no instance has both the new config and old code exposed to traffic in a way that fails yet.

**Phase 1 — 14:02 to 14:09 (7 min): onset and escalation**
First 500s appear on `POST /checkout`. Error rate goes from 0% to 34% in ninety seconds — a near-vertical ramp, not a gradual degradation. This is `v411` instances hitting the new `split` config value and throwing in `assertSettlementMode()`. By 14:09, when the page fires, error rate has climbed further to 61%, with three of the four instances now on `v412`. So for this seven-minute stretch, the failure rate roughly doubled while on-call was still becoming aware of the problem — meaning a majority of checkout attempts in the back half of this phase were failing, with essentially no mitigation in progress yet.

**Phase 2 — 14:09 to 14:14 (5 min): paged, diagnosing**
On-call is now paged and working the problem, but no config or code change has been made yet. Error rate is not reported as improving in this window — customers continue hitting the ~61% failure rate established at 14:09 while root cause is being investigated.

**Phase 3 — 14:14 to 14:21 (7 min): cause identified, not yet acted on**
On-call identifies that `PAYMENTS_SETTLEMENT_MODE` changed from `legacy` to `split`. This is a diagnosis step, not a fix — the config in production is unchanged during this window, so checkout traffic continues failing at the same ~61% rate for another seven minutes while the revert is prepared/executed.

**Phase 4 — 14:21 to 14:33 (12 min): first remediation attempt fails**
Config is reverted to `legacy` across running instances. This is the point where responders and likely customers watching status pages would expect recovery. It does not come: error rate holds at 58% — essentially unchanged from the 61% before the revert. This is the most costly phase from a trust standpoint: a fix was shipped, monitoring was watched, and the failure rate barely moved, because migration `0042` (which had run at 14:05, mid-Phase-1) had already made the `NOT NULL settlement_currency` column mandatory, so the "reverted" `legacy` code path was now failing on insert instead of on the mode assertion. Twelve full minutes elapse with customers still unable to check out, on top of the 19 minutes that preceded it.

**Phase 5 — 14:33 to 14:41 (8 min): second remediation attempt fails**
Responders attempt a full rollback to `v411`. Instances that come up on `v411` also 500, for the same schema-mismatch reason. This confirms the working hypothesis was wrong twice, not once. Error rate is not reported as moving in this window — customers remain at essentially the same failure rate (~58%) through this second failed attempt.

**Phase 6 — 14:33 to 14:41, understanding lands (root cause at 14:41)**
By 14:41 the actual causal chain (config trigger + migration making rollback impossible) is understood and a forward fix is written. Checkout is still failing at ~58% while the fix is authored — this is not instantaneous, so add this dead time to the outage total.

**Phase 7 — 14:41 to 14:47 (6 min): fix written, not yet deployed**
The forward fix (`v413`) is being built/shipped but has not reached production. Customers are still experiencing the same failure conditions as Phase 4–5.

**Phase 8 — 14:47 to ~14:49 (2 min): recovery**
`v413` deploys. Error rate returns to 0% within two minutes. This is the only phase in the entire 47-minute window where the trend line actually moves toward zero.

---

### Net assessment

- **Total duration of customer-visible failure:** ~47 minutes (14:02 onset to ~14:49 full recovery), against a stated Sev1 window of 14:02–14:47.
- **Shape of the outage, not just its length:** this was not a steady low-grade error rate. It ramped to double digits in 90 seconds, climbed further to 61%, and then — critically — **two separate remediation attempts (config revert at 14:21, full rollback at 14:33) both failed to move the needle**, holding at 58% for roughly 26 minutes (14:21–14:47) after responders believed they'd addressed the cause. That's the most damaging part of the profile: for over half the incident, the team had already intervened and customers were still failing checkout at nearly the peak rate, with no visible progress until the actual forward fix landed.
- **No indication of partial degradation** — once error rate exceeded 34–61%, this reads as most checkout attempts failing, not a slow-path/fast-path split, for the bulk of the window.

`0042_add_settlement_currency` runs, triggered by the `v412` release job as designed (migrations run after the first instance is healthy). It adds `settlement_currency char(3) NOT NULL` with no default. From this instant, every insert into `ledger_entries` must supply that column or fail — this is the detail that later makes the outage unrecoverable by simple rollback. The lock itself was brief (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for 1.2 seconds, visible as the `pg_stat_activity` spike, later ruled out as a contributing cause in its own right).

So checkouts keep failing, just now on a not-null constraint violation instead of the mode assertion. From the customer's perspective, nothing improves — same 500, same failure to complete checkout — even though on-call has just executed what looked like the fix.

**14:33–14:41 (8 min) — Second remediation attempt also fails**
On-call attempts to roll the release back to `v411` entirely. Instances that come up on `v411` also 500, for the identical schema-mismatch reason. This is 31 minutes into the outage with two remediation attempts exhausted and impact still unresolved.

**14:41–14:47 (6 min) — Root cause understood, fix written**

Forward fix `v413` deployed — kept `split` mode and the new column, dropped `NOT NULL`, backfilled existing rows with `'USD'`, then re-applied `NOT NULL` once all instances were current. Error rate returns to 0% within two minutes of deploy.

Two compounding failures during the `v412` rollout on 2026-08-21 (14:02–14:47 UTC):

1. **Trigger**: `v412`'s config bundle flipped `PAYMENTS_SETTLEMENT_MODE` from `legacy` to `split`. Instances still running `v411` code didn't recognize `split`, and `assertSettlementMode()` threw on it — causing 500s on the instances not yet upgraded.
2. **Why rollback/revert couldn't fix it**: migration `0042` ran at 14:05 (mid-rollout, before the config revert), adding a `NOT NULL` column (`settlement_currency`) with no default to `ledger_entries`. `v411`'s `chargeOrder()` never wrote that column, so once reverted to `legacy` (or rolled back to `v411`), every insert violated the new not-null constraint. The error type changed but the error rate didn't — the migration made the config trigger unrecoverable by rollback.

Fixed by `v413` (14:47), which dropped the `NOT NULL` constraint, backfilled the column, then re-applied `NOT NULL` once all instances were on `v413`.
